summary: Improve SLA tracking, payment checks, variation control, and close-out. Explore this practical post-award contract management course.
lede: Post-award contract management focuses on controlling supplier delivery, payments, changes and close-out after a contract is signed. It is for contract managers, procurement officers, project managers and commercial teams who need to verify performance and manage commercial exposure. You will practise measuring service levels, checking payment evidence, recording variations and claims risks, and escalating underperformance; Excel tracking and close-out reporting are included, while AI-assisted screening and Power BI are overview topics only.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals responsible for controlling supplier delivery, payment evidence, contract changes, and close-out across public-sector, donor-funded, and large corporate contracts. This course is designed for: Contract managers tracking obligations, deliverables, variations, and contract records. Procurement officers monitoring supplier performance against awarded contract terms. Project managers coordinating milestones, acceptance evidence, and contract dependencies. Quantity surveyors valuing completed work and reviewing payment applications. Grant and programme officers checking deliverables against funding and contract milestones. Commercial managers reviewing change exposure, claims notices, and supplier entitlements. Finance controllers matching invoices to approved milestones and acceptance evidence. Supplier-performance analysts maintaining SLA measures and performance dashboards. Contract administrators preparing notices, variation logs, and close-out records. Service-delivery managers addressing recurring supplier failures and corrective actions.
prerequisites: Working familiarity with procurement, project delivery, supplier management, or contract administration will help you apply the exercises. No coding is required. Bring access to Excel if you want to adapt the spreadsheet exercises; use anonymized records only.
